classification.difficultyReason: Requires an ordered similarity proof and combines proportional sides with the equal diagonals of an isosceles trapezium.

content.prompt: $ABCD$ is an isosceles trapezium with $AB\parallel CD$ and $AD=BC$. The diagonals of $ABCD$ intersect at $X$.

spec.description: An isosceles trapezium with a shorter upper base, both diagonals and matching single parallel arrows on the bases. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: AB is parallel to CD; AD equals BC; AC and DB intersect at X. A and B are the upper vertices, D and C the lower vertices.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens and point labels are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle ABX$ is similar to $\triangle CDX$.

answer.short:
$\triangle ABX\sim\triangle CDX$ (AAA).

Alternate angles are equal because $AB\parallel CD$, and the angles at $X$ are vertically opposite.
answer.worked:
$\angle BAX=\angle DCX$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

$\angle ABX=\angle CDX$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

$\angle AXB=\angle CXD$ (vertically opposite angles).

Therefore $\triangle ABX\sim\triangle CDX$ (AAA).

children.label: b
children.prompt: Given that $AB=4\text{ cm}$, $BX=2.5\text{ cm}$ and $DC=8\text{ cm}$, calculate:

answer.short:
$AX=2.5\text{ cm}$.

The equal diagonals of the isosceles trapezium are divided in the same ratio at $X$.
answer.worked:
The diagonals of an isosceles trapezium are equal, so $AC=BD$.

From part a, corresponding sides give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AX}{CX}&=\frac{AB}{CD}\\\frac{AX}{CX}&=\frac{4}{8}\\CX&=2AX.\end{align*}$$
Similarly, $DX=2BX$.
$$\begin{align*}AC&=AX+CX\\AC&=3AX\\BD&=BX+DX\\BD&=3BX.\end{align*}$$
Since $AC=BD$, $3AX=3BX$.
$$\begin{align*}AX&=BX\\AX&=2.5\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

Corresponding sides of the similar triangles give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{DX}{BX}&=\frac{CD}{AB}\\\frac{DX}{2.5}&=\frac{8}{4}\\DX&=2.5\times2\\DX&=5\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
